news.title: CEO称AI推广顺利，员工却不以为然——《纽约时报》
news.snippet: 《纽约时报》DealBook调查显示，企业CEO普遍认为AI推广顺利，但普通员工却持相反看法。
news.raw_snippet:
## DealBook

Surveys show workers and executives have different views on A.I.

When it comes to artificial intelligence, chief executives and their work forces aren’t seeing eye to eye.

Corporate leaders, increasingly in earnings calls and interviews, tout productivity gains and say they are doing right by their workers as they roll out the technology.

But workers are much more concerned about being supplanted, and they don’t trust their company’s executives. [...] A survey from the Milken Institute-Harris Poll Listening Project recently found that more than two-thirds of business leaders expect they will be better off financially in five years because of A.I., while just 27 percent of the U.S. work force felt the same way — a whopping 41 point gap. [...] Workers also see less A.I. transformation than leadership does. Nearly three-fourths of leaders say A.I. has significantly changed the way work is done, compared with 58 percent of entry and midlevel employees, according to a report released this month from the Wharton School.
